name: Battle of Austerlitz

phases.title: The armies take their ground
phases.text: Napoleon abandoned the Pratzen Heights and moved all his troops but the right flank into dead ground. The Allies planned four columns against the French right, with the Russian Guard in reserve and Bagration on their right.

phases.title: The Allies attack Telnitz and drive the French out
phases.text: The first Allied lines attacked Telnitz, which the 3rd Line Regiment defended. Several heavy Allied charges evicted the French from the village and forced them onto the other side of the Goldbach.

phases.title: Davout's men retake Telnitz
phases.text: The first men of Davout's corps arrived and threw the Allies out of Telnitz. Allied hussars attacked them and the Allies left the village again, and further Allied attacks out of Telnitz were checked by French artillery.

phases.title: The fight for Sokolnitz
phases.text: The second and third Allied columns attacked Sokolnitz and its castle. The French were forced out, counterattacked and regained the village, and were thrown out again until Friant's division of Davout's corps retook it.

phases.title: The Tsar orders Kutuzov off the Pratzen Heights
phases.text: Kutuzov's corps had halted on the Heights, but the Tsar ordered it to withdraw. That left the Allied centre weak.

phases.title: Soult's corps climbs the Heights
phases.text: The mist was clearing and Napoleon ordered the attack. St. Hilaire's division led the climb, and as it ascended the sun tore the mist apart. The Russians on top of the Heights were stunned to see so many French troops coming.

phases.title: The Allies drive the French back down the slope
phases.text: Allied commanders brought some delayed detachments of the fourth column into the struggle, and men of the second column joined them. After over an hour of fighting they forced the French to withdraw down the slopes.

phases.title: The French bayonet the Allies off the Heights
phases.text: Gripped by desperation, St. Hilaire's men struck hard again and bayoneted the Allies out of the Heights, and the Allied IV Corps fell back from them.

phases.title: The Russian Guard counterattacks
phases.text: Grand Duke Constantine's Guard counterattacked in Vandamme's section, forcing a bloody effort and taking a French standard. Napoleon sent in his heavy Guard cavalry, and with large masses of cavalry on both sides no victory was clear.

phases.title: The Russian Guard breaks
phases.text: Drouet's division deployed on the flank and let the French cavalry rally behind it. The horse artillery of the Guard hurt the Russian cavalry and fusiliers, and the Russians broke and were pursued for about a quarter of a mile.

phases.title: Liechtenstein's cavalry is beaten in the north
phases.text: Liechtenstein's heavy cavalry attacked Murat's lighter cavalry. Caffarelli's infantry halted the Russian assaults, and Murat sent in two cuirassier divisions, which won the long and bitter mêlée.

phases.title: Lannes drives Bagration off the field
phases.text: On Napoleon's orders Lannes led his corps against Bagration's men and, after hard fighting, drove Bagration off the field. Napoleon called off a pursuit.

phases.title: Sokolnitz falls and the Allied army leaves the field
phases.text: St. Hilaire's division and part of Davout's corps broke through at Sokolnitz. The commanders of the first two columns fled, and general panic seized the Allied army, which abandoned the field in all possible directions.

note: North is drawn at the top because the Olmütz/Brno road ran east to west and the Goldbach flowed south. The French are drawn in the west and the Allies in the east; the accounts do not say exactly where each village and stream lay, so they are placed by judgement. Where the French reserve lay is not stated. St. Hilaire's division is treated as part of Soult's corps, as its attack on the Pratzen Heights suggests. The routes of the Allied cavalry and of the fleeing columns are not given. The Satschan ponds episode is disputed and is not drawn.
